phases.phase-6: First Steps: pregnant through the first act, delivering Franklin in zero-g mid-escape from Galactus, and carrying the film's spine — she's the one who rallies a terrified Earth to stand together. In the climax she pours everything into shoving Galactus through the portal and dies for it; Franklin, in her arms, brings her back.

characters.name: Johnny Storm / Human Torch
characters.description: Sue's hotheaded (literally) pilot brother.

phases.phase-6: First Steps: the flyboy who takes the Silver Surfer personally — he obsesses over her broadcasts, decodes her language, and learns the herald was once a person who traded herself for her world. Talking to her in her own tongue is what cracks her loyalty to Galactus. Less 'flame on,' more first contact.

characters.name: Ben Grimm / The Thing
characters.description: The Fantastic Four's rock-skinned strongman with the softest heart on the team.

phases.phase-6: First Steps: the pilot who paid the cosmic-ray bill with his skin, now Earth-828's favorite uncle — Yancy Street's own, gently courting a schoolteacher, and first through every wall when Galactus comes. It's clobberin' time gets said. It's earned.

characters.name: Silver Surfer
characters.description: A chrome-skinned herald riding ahead of something world-ending.

phases.phase-6: First Steps: Shalla-Bal, the herald who marks Earth for her master's hunger — and who once was a person who gave herself to Galactus to spare her own world. Johnny's refusal to treat her as a monster, in her own language, is what turns her; when it counts, she breaks from Galactus and helps end his feast.

characters.name: Thanos
characters.description: The Mad Titan — a warlord pursuing all six Infinity Stones with a terrifying sense of purpose.

phases.phase-1: The Avengers' credit scene turns the whole invasion into a job interview: the throne behind Loki's army turns and smiles at the words 'to court Death.'
phases.phase-2: Guardians of the Galaxy shows him holding court — Ronan's patron, Gamora and Nebula's 'father' — until Ronan keeps the stone for himself. Age of Ultron's tag is him done delegating: 'Fine. I'll do it myself.'
phases.phase-3: Infinity War makes him the protagonist of his own film: six stones in two days, trading the only thing he loves on Vormir, and winning. The snap. Endgame then kills him twice — the broken farmer beheaded by Thor in the first twenty minutes, and the 2014 variant who reads the future, comes forward for round two, and dusts mid-smirk at Tony's snap.

characters.name: Ultron
characters.description: Tony Stark's peacekeeping AI gone horribly right: it looked at the data and decided humanity was the threat.

phases.phase-2: Age of Ultron: alive for minutes before concluding the mission ('peace in our time') requires extinction. He builds a body, an army, a floating city-meteor, and a philosophy — quoting Pinocchio the whole way. His intended perfect body wakes up as the Vision instead, and it's the Vision who shuts the last of him off, almost kindly.

characters.name: Hela
characters.description: The Goddess of Death, whose return spells doom for Asgard.

phases.phase-3: Ragnarok: Odin's firstborn and original executioner — the empire's dirty secret, painted over literally, in the palace murals. Released by his death, she crushes Mjolnir like a stress ball, takes Asgard in an afternoon, and can only be stopped by the apocalypse itself: Thor starts Ragnarok on purpose, and Surtur brings the whole kingdom down on her.

characters.name: Red Skull
characters.description: Head of HYDRA, the Nazi deep-science division, and the first super-soldier experiment gone wrong.

phases.phase-1: The First Avenger: Erskine's formula plus an unworthy man — Johann Schmidt, who took HYDRA private and tried to out-evil the Nazis. Grabbing the Tesseract bare-handed doesn't kill him; it relocates him.
phases.phase-3: Where to, Infinity War answers: Vormir, cursed to be the Soul Stone's ghostly tour guide — condemning Thanos' sacrifice of Gamora, then Endgame's Vormir scene with Natasha and Clint. The stone he chased for a lifetime, and he can never touch it.

characters.name: Helmut Zemo
characters.description: A meticulous Sokovian mastermind who despises what super-people cost the world.

phases.phase-3: Civil War: no powers, no army — just patience. A Sokovian colonel who lost his family under Ultron's meteor, he frames Bucky, resurrects one buried tape, and splits the Avengers with the truth. The only villain of the era whose plan simply works.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: sprung for the Flag-Smasher hunt, he brings a purple mask, a Sokovian fortune, and the era's most GIF'd dance. Still convinced super-soldiers are a mistake; still not entirely wrong. The Dora Milaje escort him to the Raft.

characters.name: Erik Killmonger
characters.description: A black-ops soldier with a righteous grievance and a claim on Wakanda's throne.

phases.phase-3: Black Panther: N'Jadaka, the cousin Wakanda abandoned in Oakland after T'Chaka killed his father. He wins the throne fair by Wakandan law — that's the sting — and his plan is his father's dream weaponized: vibranium for every oppressed people on Earth. T'Challa beats the man but keeps the question. 'Bury me in the ocean, with my ancestors that jumped from the ships.'
phases.phase-5: Wakanda Forever: waiting on the ancestral plane when Shuri burns the herb — exactly the ancestor her vengeance deserves, asking whether she'll be noble like her brother, or like him.

characters.name: Ulysses Klaue
characters.description: A cackling arms dealer and one of the only outsiders to have seen the real Wakanda.

phases.phase-2: Age of Ultron: the black-market source of stolen vibranium, paid in billions and one severed arm when he compares Ultron to Stark.
phases.phase-3: Black Panther: sonic-cannon arm, karaoke-villain energy, and the truth the world isn't ready for — 'a mining tribe? It's El Dorado.' Killmonger uses him as an entry ticket: a Wakandan body to present at the border.

characters.name: Adrian Toomes / Vulture
characters.description: A blue-collar salvager turned winged, high-tech arms dealer.

phases.phase-3: Homecoming: the cleanup contractor Stark's Damage Control squeezed out, who kept the alien salvage and built a business. The car-ride reveal — he's Liz's dad, doing the math on Peter mid-drive — is the era's best villain scene. He ends in prison, keeping Peter's identity to himself. A debt's a debt.

characters.name: Quentin Beck / Mysterio
characters.description: A caped hero who claims to have come from another Earth.

phases.phase-4: Far From Home: the multiverse claim is theater — Beck is a fired Stark illusion-engineer running a con with drones, projectors, and a disgruntled-employee support group. He plays mentor to grieving Peter to inherit EDITH, nearly wins, and weaponizes his death: the posthumous deepfake outs Peter's identity and frames him for murder. That lie is the doorway No Way Home walks through — every consequence in it traces back to Beck's parting shot.

characters.name: Xu Wenwu
characters.description: The immortal holder of the Ten Rings and leader of the criminal empire named for them — Shang-Chi's father.

phases.phase-4: Shang-Chi: a thousand years of conquest, one decade of retirement for love — and when Li died, the rings went back on and the children got an assassin's education. The film's tragedy is that his villainy is grief: the Dweller-in-Darkness wears his dead wife's voice, and he tears open Ta Lo's gate to reach her. His last act is passing the rings to his son. (He'd also like a word about the fake 'Mandarin' who borrowed his organization's name.)

characters.name: Gorr the God Butcher
characters.description: A grieving zealot armed with a god-killing blade.

phases.phase-5: Love and Thunder: the last believer on a dead world, whose god laughed at his daughter's grave — so the Necrosword found a perfect hand. His crusade drags Thor through kidnapped children and a shadow realm to Eternity's altar, where he gets one wish... and, talked down by two dying Thors, spends it not on deicide but on his daughter, alive again. Thor inherits the kid.

characters.name: Namor
characters.description: The winged-ankled king of a hidden undersea civilization.

phases.phase-5: Wakanda Forever: K'uk'ulkan, the feathered serpent god — a centuries-old mutant born of the same vibranium desperation that hid Wakanda, ruling Talokan, the ocean's answer to it. The surface world's vibranium hunt makes him strike first: he floods Wakanda's capital and kills its queen. Shuri beats him and spares him — and his tag-scene smile says the concession was strategy: let Wakanda absorb the world's anger first.

characters.name: Kang
characters.description: A conqueror with mastery over time — and countless variants of himself scattered across the multiverse.

phases.phase-4: Loki reveals the original: He Who Remains, the variant who won the multiwar and caged every timeline into one to keep his other selves out. Sylvie's blade frees them all. Quantumania: Kang the Conqueror, the exiled variant Janet met — timeline-eraser, civilization-farmer, beaten in the Quantum Realm by ants and Langs and left to his own collapsing engine. The tag shows the real problem: a stadium of Kangs, annoyed. Season two rewinds his echo — Victor Timely, a nineteenth-century inventor with the same face and none of the menace.

characters.name: The High Evolutionary
characters.description: A god-playing scientist obsessed with engineering a perfect society, no matter the cost.

phases.phase-5: Vol. 3: the Sovereign's creator, Counter-Earth's landlord, and the hand that built Rocket — cage by cage, friend by friend — then marked him property when the experiment out-thought its maker. No redemption arc, no tragic backstory: just vivisection dressed as vision. Rocket leaves him beaten, breathing, and irrelevant.

characters.name: Taskmaster
characters.description: A masked operative who can perfectly mimic any fighting style after seeing it once.

phases.phase-3: Black Widow: the Red Room's mirror-fighter — and its cruelest secret. Under the mask is Antonia Dreykov, the daughter Natasha's defection bombing maimed, rebuilt by her father into a photographic-reflex weapon. The antidote frees her with the rest of the Widows.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: recruited into Val's containment-room cleanup — and killed in the opening crossfire, the film's first lesson in how disposable the roster is.

characters.name: Ava Starr / Ghost
characters.description: A woman phasing painfully in and out of solid reality thanks to a childhood quantum accident.

phases.phase-3: Ant-Man and the Wasp: the lab accident that killed her parents left her molecularly unstable — every day is pain, and S.H.I.E.L.D. turned the condition into a stealth asset before discarding her. She hunts the Pyms' tunnel not for power but relief; Janet's returned energy steadies her.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: phasing steadier now, on Val's deniable-asset payroll — until the containment-room trap. She walks out a founding New Avenger, which nobody is more surprised by than her.

characters.name: Emil Blonsky / Abomination
characters.description: A soldier whose super-serum experiment went monstrous — later trying, sincerely or not, to reform.

phases.phase-1: The Incredible Hulk: a career commando who chased the Hulk's power through serum and Banner's blood into becoming the Abomination — wrecking Harlem until the Hulk chokes him down.
phases.phase-4: Reappears cage-fighting Wong in Shang-Chi (they have an arrangement), then She-Hulk makes him a case file: Jen's client at his parole hearing, running a wellness retreat with seven soul mates and a lot of haiku. The reform is genuine-ish; the paid Abomination appearances violating parole are also real. Back to the Raft, zen intact.

characters.name: Thaddeus Ross
characters.description: The hard-line general who hunted the Hulk, whose political career keeps on climbing.

phases.phase-1: The Incredible Hulk: the general who made Banner a fugitive — and whose daughter Betty loved him. His serum program built the Abomination; his hunt built the monster's audience.
phases.phase-3: Civil War: now Secretary of State, delivering the Sokovia Accords ultimatum and jailing half the team when they refuse. Spends Infinity War being righteously ignored.
phases.phase-6: Brave New World: President Ross, trying to be better than his record while Sterns — the gamma genius he's secretly imprisoned and exploited for years — detonates it from inside: the pills keeping Ross alive turn him into the Red Hulk on live television. He ends the film resigned, imprisoned, and — for the first time — honest, with Betty visiting.

characters.name: Valentina Allegra de Fontaine
characters.description: A silky Washington power broker quietly recruiting "assets" for purposes unknown.

phases.phase-3: Black Widow's credit scene introduces the shopping spree: at Natasha's grave, she hands Yelena a target — Clint Barton.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: materializes beside a court-martialed John Walker with a card that isn't printed yet and the title 'U.S. Agent.' Wakanda Forever confirms the day job: Director of the CIA, and Everett Ross's ex-wife, arresting him personally.
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: her ledger comes due — the containment-room trap was her shredding evidence, personnel included. When the survivors walk out alive with Bob in tow, she pivots mid-press-conference: meet 'the New Avengers.' She creates the team by failing to kill it.

characters.name: Erik Selvig
characters.description: An astrophysicist, Jane Foster's mentor, and one of the first scientists on Earth to treat Asgard as a physics problem rather than a myth.

phases.phase-1:
Thor: a colleague of Jane's father who thinks her Einstein-Rosen bridge research is a career-ender, right up until a man falls out of the sky. He is the one who gets Thor out of S.H.I.E.L.D. custody, and by the mid-credits Loki is already standing behind him, telling him what to say about the Tesseract.

The Avengers: taken by Loki in the opening scene and put under the sceptre's control. He is the reason the portal works, having built the device that stabilises the Tesseract on top of Stark Tower, and also the reason it can be closed, because he built in a failsafe while he was under and left Loki's own sceptre as the way to shut it. He is snapped out of it when Selvig is knocked unconscious.
phases.phase-2: Thor: The Dark World: has not recovered from being used. He was institutionalised after New York and turns up lecturing at Stonehenge with no trousers on, which the film plays for laughs and then quietly takes seriously. His gravimetric spikes are what let them fight through the Convergence at all, and they are the closest thing anyone has to a working theory of the nine realms.
phases.phase-4: He stops appearing after Phase Three, but his work does not stop being used. Spider-Man: Far From Home refers back to him, which is the point at which his research has outlived his own involvement in it.
phases.phase-5: Ms. Marvel: name-checked again by Bruno, Kamala's friend, in a scientific context. Two mentions across two phases, from characters with no connection to each other, which is a reasonable measure of how much of Earth's understanding of this stuff started with him.

characters.name: Dane Whitman
characters.description: A history professor at the Natural History Museum in London, and the closest thing Sersi has to a normal life.

phases.phase-4: Eternals: Sersi's boyfriend, kept outside the plot for most of the film and told the truth about her only once there's no way around it. He takes it about as well as anyone could. The post-credits scene is the point of him: he opens an old case containing the Ebony Blade, a sword with his family name on it, and an unseen voice asks whether he's sure he's ready for that. Nothing has been done with him since.

characters.name: Eros / Starfox
characters.description: A Titan-born Eternal with more charm than sense, who turns up looking for the members of the team who went missing.

phases.phase-4: Eternals: arrives in the mid-credits aboard Ted the ship, introduced by Pip the Troll as the prince of Titan and Thanos's brother. He tells the remaining Eternals he knows where their captured friends have been taken and offers to help get them back. That thread has not been picked up since.

characters.name: Khonshu
characters.description: The Egyptian god of the moon, who speaks through a chosen avatar and is only ever heard by the person he has chosen.

phases.phase-4: Moon Knight: the voice in Marc Spector's head and the source of his powers, kept alive by a bargain Marc made when he was dying. Khonshu wants wrongdoers punished, and the other gods have no patience for how he goes about it, so they seal him in stone partway through. He is not a benevolent patron. He picked Marc partly because a fractured mind is easier to steer, he threatens to take Layla as a replacement, and the final scene reveals he kept a third personality, Jake Lockley, as his own avatar the whole time, doing the killing Marc refused to do.

characters.name: Victor Timely
characters.description: An inventor and showman at the turn of the twentieth century, selling machines that are far too advanced for the year he's selling them in.

phases.phase-4: First glimpsed in the Quantumania post-credits, lecturing to a small crowd in 1901 while Loki and Mobius watch from the back. In Loki season two he's the man they need: a variant of He Who Remains, working from a technical manual that Ravonna Renslayer and Miss Minutes handed to him as a child, which makes him the only person alive who can repair the Temporal Loom. He is nothing like the version who built the TVA. He's nervous, decent and badly out of his depth, and he's killed on the gangway by temporal radiation before he can finish the job.

characters.name: Bob Reynolds / Sentry
characters.description: A quiet man with a history of addiction and depression, who volunteered for something he didn't understand.

phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: Valentina's real project, and the reason she wanted the rest of the team dead. Bob was a test subject in a programme meant to reproduce the super-soldier serum, and it worked far past anyone's intention, leaving him with something close to unlimited power. The problem is that it came with the depression rather than instead of it. His low is a separate thing called the Void, which blacks out Manhattan and pulls people into their own worst memories, and it can't be fought, only talked down. The team reaches him rather than beating him, which is the whole argument of the film.

characters.name: John Walker
characters.description: The government's hand-picked replacement Captain America — a decorated soldier in over his head.

phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: three Medals of Honor and none of Erskine's 'good man' test. Handed the shield by committee, he takes the serum under pressure and — after losing his partner — executes a surrendering Flag-Smasher with it on camera. Stripped of the title, he resurfaces as Val's 'U.S. Agent.'
phases.phase-6: Thunderbolts*: a merc with a failing marriage and the era's biggest chip on his shoulder, thrown into Val's trap with people he'd normally fight. The Void forces him through his worst self; he comes out something like a teammate. New Avenger, asterisk earned.

characters.name: Gravik
characters.description: A young Skrull revolutionary leading a rogue faction that's done waiting for a new homeworld.

phases.phase-5: Secret Invasion: radicalized by Fury's broken promise, he runs the rebellion from a repurposed reactor — false-flag bombings, a Super-Skrull program built from harvested Avengers DNA, and infiltrators as deep as War Machine's armor. G'iah, powered by the same Harvest he sought, kills him in the finale.

characters.name: Parker Robbins / The Hood
characters.description: A charismatic Chicago crew leader who recruits Riri Williams for a string of high-tech heists, and whose gear works better than it has any right to.

phases.phase-5: Recruits Riri into his crew in Ironheart, offering her the funding her armour needs — and turning out to be powered by a cloak whose bargain runs on something far older and hungrier than technology. His pull on Riri is the season's real conflict: he offers her everything she says she wants, at a price she keeps agreeing to pay.

characters.name: Cassandra Nova
characters.description: A bald, terrifying telepath ruling a wasteland at the edge of existence.

phases.phase-4: Deadpool & Wolverine: Charles Xavier's twin sister, dumped in the Void as an infant and grown into its warlord — a telepath who walks her fingers through people's skulls for fun. Wade and Logan's road trip runs straight through her court; ending her costs them most of a universe's worth of trouble.

characters.name: Galactus
characters.description: A cosmic entity that devours entire worlds.

phases.phase-6: First Steps: the Devourer of Worlds arrives at Earth-828 with one alternative to consumption — hand over baby Franklin, whose potential he wants as a vessel for his hunger. The Four refuse, bait him across the planet, and shove him through a teleport portal at the cost of Sue's life (briefly). He does not die. Entities like this don't.

characters.name: Ego
characters.description: Peter Quill's charming, mysterious, very long-lost father.

phases.phase-2: Vol. 2: a Celestial — a living planet wearing a Kurt Russell — who seeded children across the galaxy to grow a second expansion-node, and killed every one that failed him. He also, by his own cheerful admission, put the tumor in Meredith Quill's head. Peter stops being his battery and the family detonates him from the core out.

characters.name: Ronan the Accuser
characters.description: A Kree fanatic wielding a war hammer and an apocalyptic grudge.

phases.phase-3: Captain Marvel (1995): a decade-younger Ronan leads the Accusers' bombardment of Earth until Carol swats his missiles — and his fleet — out of the sky personally. 'We'll be back for the weapon.' He means her.
phases.phase-2: Guardians of the Galaxy: the zealot who breaks his deal with Thanos the moment the orb shows him what's inside — planet-killing power in his hammer and Xandar in his sights. He's undone by a dance-off and a held hand.

characters.name: Ebony Maw
characters.description: A member of the Black Order gifted with telekinetic abilities and loyal servant to the mad Titan Thanos.

phases.phase-3: Following his involvement in the massacre of half the Asgardian race, Maw was sent to Earth with Cull Obsidian to seize the Time Stone, a mission that culminated in him abducting and torturing Doctor Strange to break his protective enchantments. His campaign was cut short aboard his own spaceship, where a rescue exploit by Iron Man blew Maw out into the deadly vacuum of open space, ending his life.

characters.name: Cull Obsidian
characters.description: A member of the Black Order and loyal servant to the mad Titan Thanos.

phases.phase-3: Helped Thanos to gather all the Infinity Stones. He fought against the Avengers on earth after attacking the ship carrying the homeless Asgardians. He receoved a prosthetic arm after losing his original against Iron Man, Doctor Strange, Wong, and Spider-Man. He was later killed by Banner in their attack on Wakanda.

characters.name: The Collector
characters.description: A cosmic entity who collects rare and valuable items from across the universe.

phases.phase-2: The Collector, whose real name is Taneleer Tivan, set up his famous museum on Knowhere, a busy space station built inside a giant mining colony. His obsession with finding the Infinity Stones started in 2013 when the Asgardians gave him the Reality Stone to keep safe. The next year, he tried to buy the Power Stone from the Guardians of the Galaxy, but that deal fell apart completely.
phases.phase-3: in 2018 when Thanos attacked Knowhere, wrecked the place, and stole the Reality Stone. After everyone was brought back from the Blip, Tivan decided to leave it all behind and sold what was left of Knowhere to the Guardians of the Galaxy.

characters.name: Georges Batroc / Batroc the Leaper
characters.description: A French mercenary and pirate for hire, quick enough on his feet to go hand to hand with a super soldier.

phases.phase-2: The Winter Soldier: hijacks the Lemurian Star with a crew of pirates and takes its engineers hostage, which is what puts Steve and Natasha on board in the first place. Steve goes at him hand to hand on deck and loses the mask doing it. Batroc ends the film in custody.
phases.phase-4: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier: out again and running the hijacking Sam breaks up over Tunisia in the first episode, gone by parachute before Sam can get hold of him. Karli Morgenthau hires him with the Power Broker's own money for the fight in New York. He works out who has been paying him all along, tries to sell that back to her, and Sharon Carter shoots him for it.
